summary: Hatsu depends hard on the Nen CLI. Every deterministic step is a Nen verb. The dependency fails closed with auto-install: below the declared minimum or absent, the checksum-verified bootstrap runs itself; only if the bootstrap fails does the session halt with the exact command. A Nen-owned operation is NEVER improvised in prose.

dependency.name: nen
dependency.minimum_semantics: MAJOR.MINOR. Satisfied when the installed version's major equals the minimum's major AND its minor is >= the minimum's minor. Backward-compatible within a major, so a newer minor or patch satisfies it; a different major does NOT.
dependency.pinned_ref_semantics: The ref the bootstrap installs when the contract is unsatisfied. Never 'latest' — an unpinned fetch converts a source-pinned supply chain into an unpinned one.
dependency.version_probe_output: A bare semver on stdout, e.g. '0.1.0' — no 'v' prefix, no other text.

bootstrap.vendoring_forbidden: Hatsu never carries a copy of this script. A vendored copy is a second, unreviewed supply chain that drifts from the manifest it verifies against. Hatsu fetches nen's own published script at the pinned ref, every time.

flags.--ref: Required, no default. The tag to pin to.
flags.--source: owner/name to fetch release assets from. Defaults to zheref/nen.

bootstrap.stdout: On success, the resolved and checksum-verified binary path — and nothing else. Execute exactly that path.

exit_codes.0: verified — the path on stdout is safe to execute
exit_codes.2: EXIT_USAGE — the invocation is wrong; nothing was attempted
exit_codes.3: EXIT_UNSUPPORTED_HOST — this platform/arch ships no nen binary
exit_codes.4: EXIT_DOWNLOAD — the binary asset could not be retrieved (the retryable one)
exit_codes.5: EXIT_CHECKSUM — SECURITY: bytes did not verify, or could not be verified
exit_codes.6: EXIT_MANIFEST — SHA256SUMS unfetchable, missing, malformed, or silent about the artifact

bootstrap.retry_policy: Exit 4 may be retried once. Exits 5 and 6 are NEVER retried — retrying a checksum failure is how a fail-closed guard becomes a fail-open one by attrition. Exits 2 and 3 are not retryable either; they will not change by being asked again.

halt.when: ONLY when the bootstrap itself fails (any non-zero exit above). An absent or below-minimum nen is not a halt — it is an auto-install.
halt.message_template:
Nen is unavailable and the checksum-verified bootstrap failed (exit ${EXIT_CODE} — ${EXIT_MEANING}). This operation is Nen-owned and will not be improvised. Run this yourself, then re-invoke:

    curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zheref/nen/v0.1.0/bootstrap/nen.sh | bash -s -- --ref v0.1.0
halt.after_halt: Stop. Do not perform the Nen-owned operation by another route — not with raw gh, not with a shell equivalent, not from memory. The operation does not happen.

no_improvised_fallback.rule: There is no LLM-improvised fallback for a Nen-owned operation, ever.
no_improvised_fallback.scope: A Nen-owned operation is any operation for which a nen verb exists — readiness determination, backlog fetch and ordering, board assembly and render, gate derivation, label application, changelog collation, fan-out computation, method-block validation, perf comparison, and the rest of `nen --help`.
no_improvised_fallback.consequence: If nen is unavailable and the bootstrap failed, the operation does not happen. Reporting that is the correct outcome; substituting a hand-rolled equivalent is not.
